You are a strict faithfulness evaluator for a cybersecurity RAG system. Question: What conditions are required for Password Cracking in the knowledge base? Retrieved context the answer was supposed to be grounded in: [Source 1] ## Attack description An adversary tries every possible value for a password until they succeed. A brute force attack, if feasible computationally, will always be successful because it will essentially go through all possible passwords given the alphabet used (lower case letters, upper case letters, numbers, symbols, etc.) and the maximum length of the password. ## Execution flow [Source 2] Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.(Citation: TrendMicro Pawn Storm Dec 2020) Without knowledge of the password for an account or set of accounts, an adversary may systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism.(Citation: Dragos Crashoverride 2018) Brute forcing passwords can take place via interaction with a service that will check the validity of those credentials or [Source 3] numbers, special characters, etc.).Determine account lockout policy (a strict account lockout policy will prevent brute force attacks).

Exploit

  1. Brute force password: Given the finite space of possible passwords dictated by the password policy determined in the previous step, try all possible passwords for a known user ID until application/system grants Generated answer to evaluate: The conditions required for password cracking, specifically through brute force attacks, include: 1. **Knowledge of the Password Policy**: Understanding the finite space of possible passwords dictated by the password policy (e.g., allowed characters, length) is essential for determining which passwords to attempt [Source 3]. 2. **Access to Password Hashes or Accounts**: Adversaries may need to obtain password hashes or have accounts for which they do not know the passwords. This allows them to systematically guess passwords using brute force techniques [Source 2]. 3. **Account Lockout Policy**: The effectiveness of brute force attacks can be influenced by the account lockout policy in place. A strict account lockout policy can prevent successful brute force attacks by locking accounts after a certain number of failed attempts [Source 3]. These conditions create an environment where password cracking can be attempted effectively.
